prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Customer Onboarding Field Validation Rules (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Field" · longest unbreakable word 126px · one-line width 126px
  col 2: header "Pattern" · longest unbreakable word 114px · one-line width 1074px
  col 3: header "Example valid" · longest unbreakable word 167px · one-line width 264px
  col 4: header "Error message" · longest unbreakable word 157px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A developer/QA reference sheet: for each onboarding form field it gives the validation regex, a valid sample, and the message shown on failure — a lookup table read row by row while implementing or testing one field.","reading":"Readers arrive knowing the field name (or scan the Field column as an index), then move right to the pattern, check it against the example, and read the error copy. Comparison happens within a row, not down a column, so each row must read as a single unit and the Field column must stay a stable anchor; the regex is the densest, most consulted content and the error text is the only true prose.","groups":["col 1 Field is the row key and stands alone — it is the lookup handle and must remain visually distinct and unbroken","col 2 Pattern + col 3 Example valid form a spec pair: the rule and a value that satisfies it, read together and verified against each other","col 4 Error message is the outcome/consequence text, the only column of ordinary prose, and can wrap freely without losing meaning"],"keep_intact":["field identifiers such as account_email, postal_code_us, currency_amount, eu_vat_id (no mid-word breaks)","regex anchors and atoms: ^, $, \\d{7,14}, [A-Za-z0-9._!...], (?:-\\d{4})? — break only at |, (, [, { boundaries, never inside a character class or quantifier","example values such as an email address or 2024-01-15 (break at @ or - at worst)"],"may_wrap":["error-message sentences — natural prose, wraps at word spaces with no loss","long regex alternation/branch sequences — wrap between groups, not inside them","header labels 'Example valid' and 'Error message' over two lines"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[147,100,55,57],"idea":"Field-anchored squeeze that fits 360px: every field identifier stays on one line so rows are instantly scannable, and the pattern/example/error columns absorb the cost as tall multi-line cells."},{"name":"B","widths":[120,145,45,49],"idea":"Pattern-led squeeze that fits 360px: the regex is the most-consulted artifact, so it gets the widest column while field names break at their underscores and the example/error cells wrap hard."},{"name":"C","widths":[150,480,120,170],"idea":"Deliberate horizontal scroll (920px): field intact, each regex readable in one to three lines and each error message in a few, trading a scroll gesture for a short, low-row-height table."}]}
